trips.title: Vienna, The Ring and Everything Behind It
trips.summary: Seven days of Vienna organised one district at a time, from Ringstrasse historicism to Ottakring's market streets and the Steinhof hill.

trips.title: Antwerp, With a Day in Ghent
trips.summary: A week in Antwerp taken district by district, Rubens, the diamond and fashion quarters, the docks, Zurenborg, with one full day in Ghent.

trips.title: Sofia and Plovdiv: A Split Week Between Serdica and Philippopolis
trips.sub: Sofia Valley & the Upper Thracian Plain
trips.summary: Two cities, one week, one train. Sofia is a capital built on top of its own Roman street grid, where you change metro lines through 4th-century foundations and the mineral water still runs free from a public tap.…

trips.title: Brno, Functionalism, Cellars and Café Tables
trips.summary: A slow week in Czechia's second city built around interwar villas, a daily cabbage market, an underground labyrinth and Moravian wine.

trips.title: Prague in Layers, Gothic, Baroque, Cubist, Functionalist
trips.summary: Prague read as four architectural centuries, one district a day, with Vinohrady and Karlín given as much weight as the Castle.

trips.title: Copenhagen by Neighbourhood Block
trips.summary: A seven-day city trip itinerary in Zealand / Øresund, Denmark.

trips.title: Tallinn: Limestone, Bastions & Telliskivi
trips.summary: A seven-day city trip itinerary in Harju County, Gulf of Finland, Estonia.

trips.title: Paris by the Block, Seven Arrondissements, Seven Days
trips.summary: Paris taken one walkable arrondissement at a time, with four days spent entirely off the museum spine and a market anchoring each district.

trips.title: Berlin, One Kiez at a Time
trips.summary: Seven days of Berlin taken district by district, from Museumsinsel to Neukölln, on one weekly BVG ticket and a lot of walking.

trips.title: Hamburg on the Water
trips.summary: A week of Hamburg read through its water: Speicherstadt, HafenCity, the Alster, the Elbe ferries and a Sunday dawn at the Fischmarkt.

trips.title: Athens Beyond the Rock: Neighbourhoods, Marble and the Saronic Light
trips.summary: Most people give Athens 36 hours and see one hill. A week lets the city separate into its actual parts: the archaeological core, the 19th-century neoclassical spine from Syntagma to Omonia, and the living neighbourhoods, Koukaki, Pangrati, Exarchia, Kypseli, where Athenians actually eat, argue and drink. This itinerary front-loads the Acropolis at first slot, then spends real time on the things people skip: the National Archaeological Museum's bronzes, Byzantine Athens, the SNFCC's Renzo Piano park, and the Saronic light at Sounion. Walking is short-distance but relentlessly uphill and downhill on marble that has been polished by two thousand years of feet.

trips.title: Districts and Domes: Seven Days in Budapest, Pest Side First
trips.sub: Budapest, Pest districts V-IX, Buda I-II, XIII and Óbuda
trips.summary: Budapest rewards a week because it is really several cities stacked on one river, a Habsburg parade ground in District V, a French boulevard in VI, a bombed-and-reoccupied Jewish quarter in VII, an interwar Bauhaus…

trips.title: Naples Vertical: Spaccanapoli, Sanità and the Bay
trips.summary: Naples is stacked, Greek grid under Roman market under Baroque church under a modern city that never stopped using any of it. This week works the vertical: the decumani of the Centro Storico and Spaccanapoli, the Rione Sanità's staircases and catacombs, Vomero above on the funicular, Chiaia along the water, and the Quartieri Spagnoli's grid climbing the hill behind Via Toledo. It is loud, dense, and rewards early starts and precise ticketing, Cappella Sansevero now admits nobody without a pre-booked slot. Pompeii or Herculaneum takes a day out on the Circumvesuviana. Come hungry and with proper shoes.

trips.title: Rome in Seven Layers: Centro Storico to EUR
trips.summary: Rome is not a city you see, it is a city you cross-section. This week takes seven cuts through it: the Baroque theatre of the Centro Storico, the imperial spine of Colosseum-Forum-Palatine, the Vatican, the Republican and Imperial sculpture at Palazzo Massimo, the working-class kitchen of Testaccio, the industrial archaeology of Ostiense, and Mussolini's white marble suburb at EUR, closing with a day at Ostia Antica, the port city that is Pompeii without the crowds. The single hardest skill is ticketing: four of the week's set pieces require timed slots bought on specific official platforms at specific moments, and the difference between doing that and not is roughly three hours of queuing per day. Walking is the transport of choice; the metro is only three lines and mostly goes where you are not.

trips.title: Pristina & Prizren: Kosovo's Two Cities in Seven Days
trips.sub: Kosovo, Pristina, Prizren & the Rugova highlands
trips.summary: Kosovo gives you two entirely different cities four days apart on the same €5 bus. Pristina is young, loud and architecturally strange, Yugoslav brutalism, a spiky National Library, an unfinished Orthodox cathedral, and the Newborn monument that gets repainted each February. Prizren is Ottoman: a river through the middle, a hillside fortress, a 17th-century mosque on the square, and a Serbian Orthodox cathedral rebuilt after 2004. Between and around them are the Gračanica and Visoki Dečani monasteries, still under protection, and the Rugova gorge. It is the cheapest week in this collection, and the least infrastructure-heavy: expect minibuses, cash, and conversations.

trips.title: Riga: Art Nouveau, Market Halls & the Daugava
trips.summary: A seven-day city trip itinerary in Riga & the Gulf of Riga, Latvia.

trips.title: Luxembourg City, Fortress and Valley
trips.summary: A week in the only capital where every bus, tram and train is free, spent climbing between a fortress plateau and the valleys 70 metres below.

trips.title: Three Capitals in One Country: Chișinău, Tiraspol and Comrat
trips.sub: Chișinău, Transnistria (de facto), and the Gagauz autonomy
trips.summary: Chișinău is a low green city of chestnut trees and heavy Soviet concrete where the wine bars are better than the buildings and dinner for two costs €20. From it you can reach two other capitals in under two hours:…

trips.title: A Riviera Week from a Monaco Base
trips.summary: Monaco is 2 km² and takes a day and a half. Base there and let the Ventimiglia-Cannes railway deliver a different Riviera town every morning.

trips.title: Amsterdam by Canal, Oost and Noord
trips.summary: A week of Amsterdam in rings: the UNESCO canal belt, the newer architecture of Oost and Noord, and the free ferries that cross the IJ.

trips.title: Kraków in Seven Days: Planty Ring, Kazimierz Nights, Nowa Huta Mornings
trips.sub: Lesser Poland (Małopolska), Kraków and the Wieliczka-Oświęcim corridor
trips.summary: Most people give Kraków a weekend and see the Cloth Hall, a dragon and a queue. Seven days is the length at which the city stops performing. You get the hejnał at 07:00 with nobody watching, a whole grey morning in…

trips.title: Lisbon on Foot: Seven Hills, Seven Days
trips.summary: Lisbon rewards people who accept that the city is a staircase. This week trades the tram-28 conveyor belt for a neighbourhood sequence: the Moorish tangle of Alfama and Mouraria, then the Pombaline grid and the literary hills of Chiado and Bairro Alto, then Príncipe Real, then the river, Belém's Manueline stonework west, Marvila's warehouse breweries east. Distances are short, gradients are not. A Sintra day breaks the week open with fog and Romantic follies. It suits travellers who want architecture and food weighted equally.

trips.title: Little Paris, Then the Bulldozers: Seven Days in Bucharest
trips.summary: Bucharest does not tidy itself up for you. A Brâncovenesc monastery church sits in a hole below street level with an office block on top of it; a 1930s Modernist apartment slab by a Dada founder faces a boulevard…

trips.title: Belgrade at the Confluence: Kafanas, Concrete and the Sava
trips.sub: Belgrade, with Vojvodina & Šumadija as gateways
trips.summary: Belgrade sits where the Sava meets the Danube and has been destroyed and rebuilt about forty times, which is why it reads as a collage rather than a set piece: Habsburg Zemun, Ottoman-then-Austrian Kalemegdan, 19th-century Stari Grad, socialist Novi Beograd across the river. This week walks all four, deliberately including the buildings most tourists ignore, the Genex Tower, the Museum of Yugoslavia's marble hush, the bomb-damaged General Staff ruins on Nemanjina. Eating is in kafanas, drinking is late and often on a river barge. Prices are the lowest of any capital in this collection. Serbia is outside the EU: budget for roaming and carry dinars.

trips.title: Two Ends of a Long Country: Bratislava and Košice in a Split Week
trips.sub: Bratislava (Staré Mesto, Petržalka, Devín) and Košice (Hlavná, Spiš)
trips.summary: Slovakia is 430 km wide and its two cities have almost nothing in common. Bratislava is a Habsburg river town wedged against two borders, with a coronation cathedral, a Secession church the colour of a swimming pool,…

trips.title: Seville Slow: Mudéjar Courtyards and Triana Nights
trips.summary: Seville is a city of interiors: the whole point is what happens behind the door, in the courtyard, under the vine. This week is built around that, the Real Alcázar's Mudéjar rooms at opening hour, Casa de Pilatos's Renaissance-Roman patio in the empty midday, the Hospital de los Venerables's sunken courtyard fountain, and Triana's tiled bar fronts across the river at night. Days follow the Andalusian clock: monuments before 12:00, a long lunch, siesta, then the city reopens at 20:00 and stays up. Distances are small and flat; the discipline is timing, not stamina. A Córdoba or Cádiz day by fast train supplies the contrast.
